children: Crude oil futures fell for a fifth consecutive session Tuesday, with Brent crude dipping below $100/bbl, following reports of a conditional Iranian offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the U.S. lifts its blockade.
Citing unnamed Iranian officials, Reuters and Japan's Kyodo news agency reported the proposal had been conveyed to Washington through mediators.

"The U.S. needs to announce that it wants to resolve the issue diplomatically, make that official, and then agree on a timeline for how the process will move forward," the Iranian official said, according to Reuters. "The U.N. General ​Assembly is a golden opportunity for the U.S. to return to diplomacy."
Crude oil continues to trade down, although off earlier lows, after Iranian state-affiliated media denied the claim.

Additionally, Saudi Arabia reportedly has restarted operations at its damaged East-West pipeline and aims to resume exports via the pipeline later this week, albeit at a reduced volume, from the Yanbu port on the Red Sea.

The pipeline, the primary Saudi alternative route for exports to bypass the disruption in the Strait of Hormuz, was shut down ​after attacks earlier this month, and the Iran-backed Houthis have attacked Saudi Arabia directly with missiles and drones while tightening their grip on the southern Red Sea.
The pipeline has the capacity to transport 7M bbl/day of oil, with ~2M bbl/day going to refineries along the Saudi west coast and the remainder available for exports.
The U.S., which bombed the Houthis for two months last year, reportedly has so far rebuffed repeated Saudi pleas to rejoin the fight.
